article_title: Social Skills Training (Early Childhood, Children with Disabilities)
citation: Social Skills Training. (2013). What Works Clearinghouse Intervention Report: Early Childhood Education Interventions for Children with Disabilities. U.S. Department of Education. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc
title: Behavioral social skills lesson pattern: instruct, model, practice, reinforce
description: The reviewed interventions share a recurring lesson structure: children are instructed on target behaviors, instructors model the behavior, children practice it with peers, and appropriate behavior is reinforced. In Guglielmo and Tryon (2001), "Instructors modeled the activities for the children using puppets and a short skit. Following this activity, children practiced the sharing skills with their peers," with reinforcement including continuous verbal acknowledgment and tangible rewards. LeBlanc and Matson (1995) similarly modeled with a puppet, had children model with a puppet and then with another child, and reinforced during a play phase.
requirements: Target behaviors must be specified (e.g., sharing, being in a group, greeting, initiating play)
Reinforcement of targeted behaviors during and after practice
constraints: In LeBlanc and Matson (1995), children engaging in inappropriate behavior were prompted toward an opposite positive behavior, with a one-minute time-out if they refused
target_learners: preschool children with disabilities or developmental delays
target_learning_goals: age-appropriate social skills such as sharing, joining a group, greeting, and initiating play
examples: Guglielmo and Tryon (2001) taught children to establish eye contact, tap children on the shoulder to gain attention, and ask to play with others
LeBlanc and Matson (1995) split each session into an approximately 15-minute instruction and modeling phase and an approximately 45-minute reinforced play phase
key_sources: Social Skills Training. (2013). What Works Clearinghouse Intervention Report: Early Childhood Education Interventions for Children with Disabilities. U.S. Department of Education. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/578

article_title: Repeated Reading
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2014). Repeated Reading: WWC Intervention Report, Students with Learning Disabilities. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc
title: Repeated reading as a flexible practice with seven variable implementation parameters
description: The report describes repeated reading not as a fixed protocol but as a practice whose implementation teachers can vary along seven parameters. As printed, "Teachers can vary" the criterion for progression to the next passage (minimum number of reads or a minimum reading rate of 85–100 words per minute), the instructional settings (teacher-directed, with same-age or cross-age peers, in groups, independently), the purpose, the materials (narrative texts, expository texts, poems, chants, songs, student- or class-written text), the modalities (silent with a tape, aloud with a model, choral, to a peer, to oneself), the length of the passage read, and the feedback provided on reading errors.
requirements: A teacher who selects passages and sets a progression criterion such as a minimum reading rate of 85–100 words per minute
constraints: The reviewed evidence covers individual delivery with a teacher in grades 5–12; the report does not rate effectiveness for the other configurations it lists
target_learners: students with learning disabilities in grades 5–12 with inadequate reading fluency
target_learning_goals: oral reading fluency
reading comprehension
examples: Settings range from teacher-directed one-on-one to work with same-age or cross-age peers, groups, or independent practice
Materials may include narrative texts, expository texts, poems, chants, songs, or text written by the student or class
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2014). Repeated Reading: WWC Intervention Report, Students with Learning Disabilities. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/576

article_title: Reading Recovery®
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, June). Reading Recovery® Intervention Report | English Language Arts Topic Area. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Reading Recovery training cascade: university-affiliated teacher training sites, teacher leaders, and certified teachers
description: Reading Recovery® sustains implementation through a three-level training infrastructure. Teacher training sites in public schools, affiliated with partnering universities, house teacher leaders who train teachers. Teacher leaders complete a yearlong training of graduate coursework and supervised practicums, and are expected to "provide initial training for up to 15 teacher candidates and provide ongoing support for 40 to 60 Reading Recovery® teachers or teachers in training annually." Teachers complete a yearlong graduate-credit training and must maintain registration by teaching at least eight students per year and participating in ongoing professional development.
requirements: Teacher leaders hold a master's degree and teaching credentials and complete a yearlong certification training
Teachers must be certified, experienced early elementary teachers and complete a year of training with graduate credit
Teachers must maintain registration by teaching at least eight students per year and attending ongoing professional development, typically no less than six sessions per school year
constraints: Neither contributing study provided details about the Reading Recovery® teacher training sites or the training of teacher leaders
Registration lapses after 1 year if teachers do not maintain the requirements
target_learners: Grade 1 students with low literacy achievement in districts implementing Reading Recovery®
target_learning_goals: Early literacy intervention delivered with training fidelity
examples: Based on survey results from one study, teacher leaders met 87% of the implementation standards, including attending 73% of training sessions and 98% of professional development sessions

article_title: eMINTS Comprehensive Program
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2020). eMINTS Comprehensive Program Intervention Report │ Teacher Excellence Topic Area. NCEE WWC 2020-011. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Four-component design of eMINTS: sequenced professional development, coaching, technology integration, and online resources
description: The report enumerates four key components of eMINTS. Sequenced professional development delivers "approximately 140 hours of professional development focused on integrating technology into the classroom and developing lessons that use inquiry-based learning" over 2 or more years. Coaching provides one-on-one classroom sessions by instructional specialists plus group coaching to build school learning communities. Technology integration supports inquiry-based instruction, differentiated learning, and assessment. Online resources supply an eMINTS portal with assessments, lesson plans, example classroom websites, and online courses.
requirements: Trained instructional specialists to deliver professional development and coaching
Individual student access to Internet-connected computers or tablets for technology integration
constraints: A shorter version, eMINTS4All, includes fewer professional development sessions and coaching visits
target_learning_goals: Inquiry-based, technology-supported instruction
Classroom assessment and classroom management
Building a community of learning in schools
examples: At the end of the first year, teachers develop a classroom website with the help of the instructional specialist as a resource for students and their families
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2020). eMINTS Comprehensive Program Intervention Report │ Teacher Excellence Topic Area. NCEE WWC 2020-011. https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/705

article_title: Building Blocksâ"¢
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, December). Building Blocks. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Building Blocks multi-context implementation pattern: whole-group, small-group, centers, computer activities, and family letters
description: The curriculum distributes mathematics learning across several classroom contexts: whole-group instruction during circle time (approximately 5–15 minutes, four or five times per week), small-group instruction with 3 to 6 children (approximately 10–15 minutes, two or three times per week), hands-on center activities, and computer activities that "automatically adjust when children progress well or need additional help." Weekly family/caregiver letters describe the mathematics and home activities. This pattern lets teachers adapt activities to children's developmental levels while other children work independently.
requirements: Teachers used the Teacher’s Edition to locate relevant activities.
Teachers received 4–8 full days of initial training, monthly 2-hour refresher classes, and on-site coaching 1–2 times a month.
constraints: Center activities were mostly free-choice, so frequency and duration varied; the content and duration of professional development varied across the studies.
target_learning_goals: early mathematics knowledge aligned to learning trajectories
examples: In the three contributing studies, children in the comparison group were taught by teachers who did not participate in Building Blocks training and did not implement the Building Blocks sessions.

article_title: Really Great Reading's Foundational Literacy Programs
citation: Really Great Reading. (2023). Really Great Reading. https://www.reallygreatreading.com
title: Deliver foundational literacy instruction with existing classroom staff and no additional personnel
description: RGR is designed so that "Classroom teachers, paraprofessionals, or tutors can deliver instruction" and "No additional staff is required." This staffing model keeps implementation feasible within existing school resources, complementing the program's emphasis on efficient instruction and minimized teacher preparation time through digital lesson delivery tools.
requirements: Delivery by classroom teachers, paraprofessionals, or tutors already present in the school
target_learners: Early elementary students receiving Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 support
target_learning_goals: Foundational reading skills including phonics and fluency
examples: The studied implementation assigned instruction to regular classroom teachers across 13 schools

article_title: PAX Good Behavior Game — Reading
citation: Evidence for Learning. (2023). PAX Good Behavior Game (Evidence Rating). https://evidenceforlearning.org
title: Team-based group contingency for behavior management
description: The PAX Good Behavior Game organizes classroom behavior management around a group contingency: students are divided into two or more teams, and when a member violates class rules "discussed and agreed upon by the students themselves", the team receives a check mark. The team with the fewest checkmarks, or all teams meeting a set criterion, receives a small privilege such as lining up first for recess. This structure is "intended to create a situation in which students encourage and assist their peers to behave appropriately".
requirements: class rules discussed and agreed upon by the students themselves
teacher monitoring of student behavior
small privileges as reinforcers
target_learning_goals: self-regulation and appropriate classroom behavior
examples: Teams receive checkmarks on a whiteboard for rule violations; the winning team or all qualifying teams receive a small privilege such as lining up first for recess.
key_sources: Evidence for Learning. (2023). PAX Good Behavior Game (Evidence Rating). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/pax-good-behavior-game-reading/

article_title: Corrective Reading — Elementary
citation: Corrective Reading. (2021). https://www.evidenceforessa.org/
title: Deliver Corrective Reading in small groups with sessions 4-5 days per week for optimal achievement gains
description: The article states the program "is most effective when taught in small groups" and that "Sessions should occur 4-5 days per week for optimal achievement gains". Delivery can occur inside or outside the regular classroom, and instructors may teach multiple groups across the school day.
requirements: Instructors may include general classroom teachers, special education teachers, intervention specialists, and paraprofessionals
constraints: The frequency recommendation reflects the article's stated conditions for optimal achievement gains, not a tested comparison in the summary
target_learners: Upper-elementary struggling readers in small intervention groups
target_learning_goals: Reading achievement gains
examples: Lesson delivery can occur within the regular classroom or outside of the regular classroom (pull-out).

article_title: Once Early-Reading Program
citation: Once Early-Reading Program: Evidence Rating Summary. (2025). https://once.org
title: Pair scripted tutoring delivered by non-specialist staff with weekly coaching based on session recordings and real-time progress data
description: The Once model makes non-specialist delivery viable by combining scripted, laptop-delivered lessons with a structured coaching loop: tutors receive weekly 30-minute coaching sessions from a consistent coach who reviews session recordings and provides targeted feedback, and a real-time data portal lets tutors, coaches, and administrators monitor student progress. This allows "staff without specialized reading instruction backgrounds to deliver sequenced lessons with fidelity". The article presents this staffing and supervision structure as integral to implementation.
requirements: A two-day, in-person training focused on the Science of Reading, the Once delivery method and model, and the Once technology, with ample time allocated for hands-on practice.
Weekly 30-minute coaching sessions from a consistent coach, plus laptop and internet access with a front-facing camera for session recording.
constraints: Coaching and data monitoring are described as components of the Once program specifically; the article does not report separate effects for the coaching component.
target_learners: PreK through first grade students receiving supplemental literacy tutoring
target_learning_goals: Early literacy skills delivered with fidelity by staff without specialized reading instruction backgrounds
examples: Tutors receive weekly 30-minute coaching sessions from a consistent Once coach who reviews session recordings and provides targeted feedback; a real-time data portal allows tutors, coaches, and administrators to monitor student progress.
key_sources: Once Early-Reading Program: Evidence Rating Summary. (2025). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/once-early-reading-program/

article_title: Building Assets Reducing Risks (BARR) — Attendance
citation: Building Assets Reducing Risks (BARR) program evidence summary. (2020). https://www.barrcenter.org
title: Sustain model implementation with multi-year sequenced professional development plus ongoing dedicated coaching
description: BARR pairs annual in-person training with continuous coaching: each school receives "two days of in-person professional development annually delivered through a sequenced, multi-year training plan," and "an average of more than 200 hours per year of personalized coaching and technical assistance." Year 1 training focuses on implementing the model; Years 2 and 3 address advanced topics such as effective team meetings, understanding trauma, reducing risky behaviors, and fostering student resilience.
requirements: A dedicated BARR coach assigned to each school providing structured weekly coaching sessions and quarterly on-site visits.
A sequenced, multi-year training plan using BARR materials and practice.
target_learners: teachers and school leaders implementing BARR
target_learning_goals: faithful implementation of the BARR model
continuous improvement and long-term sustainability
examples: BARR coordinators and administrators also join quarterly Professional Learning Community calls and attend the annual BARR National Conference.
key_sources: Building Assets Reducing Risks (BARR) program evidence summary. (2020). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/building-assets-reducing-risks-barr-attendance/

article_title: Targeted Skills Instruction (TSI)
citation: Targeted Skills Instruction Evidence Rating Review. (2025). https://www.edmentum.com
title: Gradual release session structure for small-group tutoring: direct instruction, guided practice, independent work
description: Each TSI session follows "a gradual release model of direct instruction, collaborative, guided practice and independent work with tutor support." This structures each 30-45 minute tutoring session so responsibility shifts from tutor-led instruction to collaborative and guided practice and finally independent work, with the tutor available throughout. The pattern was implemented in every session of the studied program.
requirements: A tutor supporting each phase of the session
short sessions of 30-45 minutes repeated three or more times per week
target_learners: K-12 students in small tutoring groups of 2-6
target_learning_goals: reading and math skill development
examples: TSI sessions in the New Jersey study ran three 30-40 minute sessions per week following this structure
key_sources: Targeted Skills Instruction Evidence Rating Review. (2025). https://www.edmentum.com

article_title: STEMscopes Math
citation: STEMscopes Math Evidence Summary. (2024).
title: 5E+IA instructional model with Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression
description: The program's organizing instructional pattern is the 5E+IA model: "Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate, plus Intervention and Acceleration pathways." It structures whole-group instruction, small-group differentiation, and blended learning, and follows a "Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression" that sequences mathematical representations from concrete materials to abstract symbols, with digital tools such as virtual manipulatives and PhET simulations integrated.

target_learning_goals: Mathematics concept and skill development across representational levels
examples: The curriculum embeds Intervention and Acceleration pathways alongside the five E phases

article_title: GO Tutor Corps High-Impact Math Tutoring
citation: GO Tutor Corps (Evidence Rating: Promising). (2024). GO Tutor Corps evidence summary. https://www.evidenceforessl.org/
title: Supplement classroom instruction with consistent in-school tutoring sessions that use student performance data to guide instruction
description: The article describes a tutoring model in which sessions occur during the school day, are consistent across the year, and use "student performance data to guide instruction." Tutoring is intended to supplement, not replace, regular classroom instruction, with progress monitoring tracking student progress over the school year.
requirements: A designated non-teaching staff member to manage tutors on-site during serving hours.

examples: GO Tutor Corps delivered individualized or small-group math tutoring during the school day in participating schools, with progress monitoring across the year.

article_title: Simple Solutions Learning – Standards-Based Math
citation: Simple Solutions Learning. (2025). Simple Solutions Learning evidence rating. https://www.simplesolutions.com
title: Supplement core instruction with short daily distributed review of previously taught skills to promote cumulative learning and retention
description: The article describes a design in which short, standards-aligned lessons revisit previously taught skills so that "the program's spiral structure is designed to strengthen recall and reduce learning loss by continually reintroducing previously covered content". Daily review of ten to fifteen problems in 10–15 minutes supplements, rather than replaces, the core curriculum. The evaluation associates this design with significantly greater assessment gains.
requirements: Daily implementation alongside the core math curriculum; teacher onboarding through professional development.
constraints: Evidence comes from one quasi-experimental study in grades 3–5; the design intent (retention, reduced learning loss) is stated by the program rather than separately tested.
target_learning_goals: Retention of previously taught math skills, procedural fluency, and multi-step reasoning
examples: Students completed ten to fifteen review problems per day, about 10–15 minutes, revisiting previously covered content.
key_sources: Simple Solutions Learning. (2025). Simple Solutions Learning evidence rating. https://www.simplesolutions.com

article_title: Waterford Upstart
citation: Waterford Upstart program description. (2024). https://www.waterford.org/upstart/
title: Pair home-based adaptive learning software with family coaching and progress updates
description: The program pairs its software with structured family involvement: "Each family is also assigned a coach who provides onboarding, routine-building guidance, and ongoing check-ins throughout the program period." Families also receive "weekly progress updates, simple at-home learning tips, and access to a bilingual resource library (English/Spanish) to help reinforce skills offline," supporting consistent use in home settings.
requirements: Assignment of a coach to each family for onboarding and ongoing check-ins
Weekly progress updates and at-home learning tips for families
constraints: Designed for home implementation by families of young children, not classroom-only delivery
target_learners: Children in PreK–2 and their families
target_learning_goals: Consistent daily engagement with early literacy, math, and science lessons
examples: Families receive weekly progress updates and use a bilingual English/Spanish resource library to reinforce skills offline

article_title: Waterford Upstart
citation: Waterford Upstart program description. (2024). https://www.waterford.org/upstart/
title: Short daily adaptive home-learning sessions sustained across the week
description: The program's usage pattern is short, frequent sessions: it "delivers daily 15–20 minute online lessons" and is "designed to be used consistently throughout the week," while the software "adjusts the level of support and difficulty as children demonstrate new skills." This combines brief session length, weekly regularity, and adaptive difficulty adjustment for young learners at home.
requirements: Daily access to a suitable device at home
Family support to maintain consistent weekly use
constraints: Session length and frequency as designed for PreK–2 children
target_learners: Children in PreK–2 learning at home
target_learning_goals: Early literacy, math, and science skill growth
examples: Daily 15–20 minute lessons in reading, math, and science used consistently throughout the week

article_title: STEMscopes Science
citation: STEMscopes evidence rating summary. (2024). Evidence rating: promising. https://www.stemscopes.com
title: 5E-based inquiry curriculum design with embedded formative assessment
description: The curriculum is organized around the 5E instructional model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate), pairing hands-on, inquiry-based investigations with real-world problem solving and embedded formative assessments. The article states the program is "grounded in the 5E instructional model" and is "designed to promote student engagement through interactive investigations, real-world problem solving, and embedded formative assessments."
requirements: Digital and print resources plus hands-on materials to support science instruction
constraints: Aligned to state standards, as evaluated in a Grade 5 science context
target_learning_goals: Science conceptual understanding and engagement through inquiry
examples: STEMscopes implements this pattern with interactive investigations and embedded formative assessments across digital, print, and hands-on materials.
key_sources: STEMscopes evidence rating summary. (2024). Evidence rating: promising. https://www.stemscopes.com

article_title: STEMscopes Science
citation: STEMscopes evidence rating summary. (2024). Evidence rating: promising. https://www.stemscopes.com
title: Pair digital science curricula with hands-on materials to support instruction across diverse classrooms
description: The article recommends that a digital science curriculum should not be screen-only: STEMscopes "includes digital and print resources as well as hands-on materials to support science instruction across diverse classrooms." Combining a digital platform students can access via computer or touch screen device with physical investigation materials is presented as the way the program supports varied classroom contexts.
requirements: Teachers need computer and/or touch screen devices to access the digital curriculum resources
constraints: Evaluated in an urban district Grade 5 science setting
target_learning_goals: Science achievement through inquiry-based instruction
examples: STEMscopes ships digital and print resources alongside hands-on materials, and students access a digital platform via computer or touch screen device.

article_title: Twig Science
citation: Twig Science — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2025). Imagine Learning program evidence summary. https://www.imaginelearning.com
title: 5E instructional model structure (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) as the organizing lesson pattern
description: Twig Science organizes instruction around the 5E model, which the summary spells out as "Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate." Within this structure the curriculum places student inquiry at the center, embeds science and engineering practices, and sequences multimedia-rich investigations and collaborative tasks across the phases. Built-in literacy supports are integrated rather than treated separately.
requirements: Implementation in each classroom by one instructional teacher, with optional curriculum training varying by grade level.
constraints: Alignment is stated for the Next Generation Science Standards; no other standards alignment is claimed.
target_learning_goals: Inquiry-based science understanding
Science and engineering practices
examples: The curriculum's investigations and collaborative tasks are delivered through the 5E phases across Grades K–8.
key_sources: Twig Science — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2025). Imagine Learning program evidence summary. https://evidenceforessa.org/program/twig-science/

article_title: Progress Learning – Science
citation: Progress Learning evidence summary. (2024). Progress Learning (Evidence Rating: Promising). https://www.progresslearning.com/
title: Diagnostic-driven individualized learning paths with progress monitoring and dashboards
description: The program's instructional design pattern assigns every student a learning path or plan featuring specific standards aligned to individual learning needs. Diagnostics and progress monitoring help educators identify students not performing at grade level so they can provide resources to catch up, while district and school dashboards let teachers monitor progress across subjects and grade levels and identify trends that may inform curriculum and teaching strategies.
requirements: Teachers create and share assessments and assignments and track progress through the platform
target_learners: K-12 students needing grade-level remediation or standards-aligned practice
target_learning_goals: Closing gaps for students not performing at grade level
examples: Diagnostics and progress monitoring used in Forney ISD to identify students not performing at grade level

article_title: NEW INSIGHTS into Children’s Temperament (INSIGHTS) – Family Engagement
citation: INSIGHTS into Children's Temperament. (2010). Program description and evidence summary. https://www.evidencebasedprograms.org/programs/insights-into-childrens-temperament/
title: Align educator professional development, classroom sessions, and parent education around a shared temperament framework
description: INSIGHTS works by giving the adults around the child a common framework: educators and parents each receive six self-paced lessons followed by remote facilitated sessions that help them "recognize their children's temperaments/personalities and learn strategies to reduce behavior problems and enhance social skills," while classroom sessions teach children the same temperament ideas. The article presents this three-component alignment as the program's design for improving self-regulation, classroom engagement, and teacher-student relationships.
requirements: Educators and parents complete six one-hour asynchronized and six one-hour synchronized lessons
target_learners: early elementary students and the teachers and families who support them
target_learning_goals: reducing behavior problems
enhancing social skills
improving teacher-student relationships
examples: The trial delivered the program simultaneously to students, teachers, and parents over ten weekly sessions.

article_title: I CAN Learn® Primary Mathematics
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2017, July). Primary Mathematics intervention report: I CAN Learn®. Retrieved from https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Five-part self-paced mastery lesson structure
description: I CAN Learn® lessons follow a repeating five-part design in which instruction is delivered by software and advancement is gated by demonstrated mastery. The curriculum studied included "109 lessons, each of which has a five-part format that includes a warm-up activity, lesson presentation, journal activity, guided practice, and a quiz to ensure mastery of the lesson content". Students complete lessons individually at their own pace using interactive software with a virtual teacher that presents multimodal lessons and demonstrates problem solving when students make errors, while the classroom teacher supports students with the lessons.
requirements: Computer equipment, desks, and electrical connectivity in classrooms; the developer provided maintenance and technical and instructional support to teachers
constraints: The study did not specify which edition of the curriculum was used
target_learning_goals: pre-algebra conceptual mastery
examples: In the reviewed quasi-experiment, intervention students used this lesson format as the primary source of math instruction for the entire academic school year in 12 to 14 middle schools
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2017, July). Primary Mathematics intervention report: I CAN Learn®. Retrieved from https://ies.ed.gov/ncee/wwc/InterventionReport/676

article_title: Headsprout® Early Reading
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2009). Headsprout® Early Reading (WWC Intervention Report). http://www.headsprout.com/
title: Adaptive computer-assisted early literacy pattern: adaptive instruction with performance criteria, cumulative review, and printable reinforcement materials
description: The program's instructional design combines several recurring features: the curriculum "provides individualized, adaptive instruction", responds "to a child's pattern of errors with tutorials and reviews to provide extra assistance", requires that "children must meet specific performance criteria in order to progress", builds in "cumulative review ... to help ensure retention", and pairs episodes with printed Readers whose "stories only contain material that children have learned up to that point". Teachers receive generated performance reports to monitor progress.
requirements: Computers must be available to children (a mobile computer lab in the study)
Teachers trained to respond to technology issues, access and decipher reports, and redirect students when necessary
constraints: Descriptive information was obtained from the program's website; further verification of accuracy was beyond the scope of the review
target_learners: prekindergarten and early elementary children learning to read

article_title: Pre-K Mathematics
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. (2023, September). Pre-K Mathematics. https://whatworks.ed.gov
title: Linked classroom and home caregiver-child math activity model for early mathematics
description: This instructional pattern pairs weekly teacher-led small-group classroom math activities with caregiver-child home activities linked to the classroom content. Each classroom activity includes "a core lesson as well as additional activities to tailor the lesson for lower- and higher-performing children" and scaffolding suggestions for common errors. Home packets contain the activity, manipulatives, and a bilingual caregiver letter with a picture strip depicting how to conduct the activity.
requirements: Teacher training in implementing the curriculum with fidelity and in progress monitoring, plus ongoing in-class coaching
constraints: Implemented in Head Start and state-funded preschool settings with low-income families; effects on non-mathematics domains were uncertain
target_learners: preschool children ages approximately 3.4 to 4.5 years from low-income families
target_learning_goals: early mathematics achievement and informal mathematical knowledge
examples: In the five reviewed studies, teachers implemented small-group sessions of 4–6 children lasting 15–20 minutes, twice a week for 24–29 weeks, and sent home caregiver-child activity packets every 1–2 weeks

article_title: Reading Mastery
citation: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Reading Mastery (Adolescent Literacy). http://www.mcgraw-hill.co.uk/sra/downloads/Reading%20Mastery/Reading%20Mastery%20Signature%20Edition%20Brochure.pdf
title: Reading Mastery lesson pattern: modeling, guided practice, and individual practice within scripted 30–45 minute multi-strand lessons
description: A typical Reading Mastery lesson lasts 30 to 45 minutes and includes "seven to nine short activities that encompass multiple strands of content, such as phonemic awareness, letter-sound correspondence, sounding out words, word recognition, vocabulary, oral reading fluency, or comprehension." The repeated teaching routine proceeds through modeling new content, providing guided practice, and implementing individual practice and application. Lesson scripts guide teachers, and signals and group responses keep students involved and on task while controlling lesson pacing.
requirements: Lesson scripts act as a guide for teachers
Signals and group responses are used to keep students involved and on task, and to control lesson pacing
target_learners: Elementary students in grades K–6, including struggling readers
target_learning_goals: Decoding, word recognition, vocabulary, oral reading fluency, and comprehension
examples: The program typically spans one academic year with daily lessons of this structure

article_title: Core-Plus Mathematics
citation: Core-Plus Mathematics. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Core-Plus Mathematics, High School Math. What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. http://www.wmich.edu/cpmp
title: Core-Plus multi-day lesson cycle: launch, small-group investigation, Checkpoint discussion, and independent task
description: Core-Plus units are organized around multi-day lessons cycling through instructional activities: a full-class launch of a problem situation with the teacher as "director and moderator"; small-group investigation in which students gather data, look for patterns, construct models, and make and verify conjectures with the teacher as facilitator; a whole-class Checkpoint discussion with the teacher as moderator; and an individual task with the teacher as "an intellectual coach". Materials promote collaborative small-group investigations followed by teacher-led whole-class summarizing that leads to analysis, abstraction, and further application.
requirements: Classroom configurations supporting small-group work in class and individual work outside class, with teacher roles shifting across director, facilitator, moderator, and coach
constraints: The cycle is described for the first edition of the curriculum reviewed by the WWC
target_learning_goals: Mathematical thinking, problem solving, and conceptual understanding through investigation of problem situations
examples: Lessons begin with a full-class discussion of a problem situation, then shift to investigating focused problems by gathering data, looking for patterns, constructing models and meanings, and making and verifying conjectures
key_sources: Core-Plus Mathematics. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Core-Plus Mathematics, High School Math. What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. http://www.wmich.edu/cpmp

article_title: Sound Partners
citation: Sound Partners. (2010). WWC Intervention Report: Sound Partners. What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. http://www.wri-edu.org/partners/sound-partners.htm
title: Short frequent one-to-one tutoring sessions with scripted phonics lessons and mastery checks
description: The program's instructional pattern is "30 minute sessions of one-to-one tutoring that take place four days per week throughout one school year." Each session includes from four to eight short activities, with the last 15 minutes allocated for oral reading practice in decodable texts matched to taught phonics skills. Although scripted, instruction can be adjusted to individual student needs, and tests given every 10 lessons gauge student mastery.
requirements: Tutors trained to choose a reading method (independent reading, partner reading, or echo reading) matching each student's reading skills
constraints: Tutoring is supplemental; treatment students in the reviewed studies also received typical classroom reading instruction
target_learners: Kindergarten and first-grade students at risk for reading difficulties
target_learning_goals: Applying word-level phonics skills in oral text reading
Reading fluency and accuracy
examples: In Vadasy and Sanders (2008), tutoring for both treatment groups occurred in 30-minute sessions, four days per week, for 18 weeks, one-on-one or in pairs.

article_title: Spalding’s The Writing Road to Reading
citation: Spalding's The Writing Road to Reading. (2024). Program description and evidence review. https://evidenceforesc.org/
title: Build in-house certified trainers to sustain program expertise within the school
description: The program's professional development path is designed so that schools develop internal capacity rather than relying on external support indefinitely: teachers move "along a professional development path towards becoming a trainer," and the program emphasizes "creating sustainable expertise within the school by developing in-house Spalding certified trainers who can provide continued support to colleagues." This makes ongoing coaching and fidelity monitoring locally sustainable.

A coordinator role to oversee fidelity and provide coaching

school-internal instructional expertise

article_title: EveryDay Intervention (Family Engagement)
citation: Attendance. (2018). https://www.evidenceforlearning.org
title: Attendance interventions can be delivered at scale with minimal staffing, training, and technology
description: The page specifies that the Absence Reports intervention requires minimal staffing — one district staff member supporting implementation at approximately 30 minutes per week and one district-level data staff member supporting data transfer in under 3 hours total — and that professional development is minimal, with "none required aside from the staffing requirements described above," and no technology required. This shows a low-burden delivery model can accompany a statistically significant attendance effect, making district adoption feasible without extensive training infrastructure.

constraints: Staffing estimates are as printed for this program; the page does not generalize them to other interventions

article_title: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention (Family Engagement)
citation: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention. (2024). PowerSchool Attendance Intervention program description and evidence summary. https://www.powerschool.com/
title: Teacher-mediated automated attendance messaging pattern combining dashboards, templates, and two-way family communication
description: The intervention operationalizes attendance improvement as a teacher-family communication workflow: educators monitor daily and period-level attendance and chronic absenteeism data, then use customized messaging templates with automatically populated parent or student names and real-time attendance data, delivered via two-way texting and email. Auto-translation features help administrators and treatment teachers reach parents from diverse backgrounds. This pattern reduces the time burden for school staff while keeping communication personalized and data-driven.
requirements: Access to a school or district administrative system to gather attendance data
Teachers and administrators trained via the Train-the-Trainer methodology
constraints: Effectiveness evidence comes from a semester-long RCT in 3 DC public schools with 6th-12th grade students; in-seat attendance effects were insignificant.
target_learning_goals: Increase family engagement
Support and improve student attendance
examples: Teachers in the treatment condition used the app and training to communicate with families, while control teachers communicated with parents as usual.
key_sources: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention. (2024). PowerSchool Attendance Intervention program description and evidence summary. https://www.powerschool.com/

article_title: Flashlight360
citation: Flashlight360 program description. (2024). https://flashlight360.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/23505832409499-Device-Specifications
title: Deliver actionable language data so teachers can offer constructive feedback that accelerates language development
description: The article states that "By delivering actionable data, Flashlight360 supports teachers in offering constructive feedback, a proven approach to accelerating language development." The principle is that progress-monitoring tools should give teachers actionable data on specific language areas so feedback can be focused and meaningful for both teachers and students working toward proficiency.

examples: Flashlight360 delivers scoring and feedback across five areas of speaking and three areas of writing to guide teacher and student efforts toward proficiency.

article_title: Renzulli Learning

critical thinking
creativity
21st-century skills
equitable opportunities

article_title: OnYourMark

title: Pair students with a consistent tutor at a small student-tutor ratio to build positive tutoring relationships

article_title: BookNook
citation: BookNook: Evidence Rating Strong. (2023). https://www.booknook.org
title: Keep the same tutor and small student group together so the tutor can learn each student's strengths and skill gaps
description: BookNook assigns students so that "students meet with the same tutor and small group of students to build relationships and to facilitate the tutor to develop an understanding of each student's strengths and skill gaps." article_title: Hoot Reading – MTSS Tier III
citation: Hoot Reading — Evidence Summary. (2025). https://www.hootreading.com
title: Deliver one-to-one tutoring through a purpose-built web application requiring only standard student devices

A web application accessible via an internet browser

Dashboards for school- and district-level monitoring

45-60 minutes per day
Six to eight weeks of implementation
Teacher(s) or interventionists staffing the stations

word-solving
fluency
writing

article_title: Strategic Adolescent Reading Intervention (STARI)

citation: Early Literacy and Learning Model (ELLM/Plus). (2008). Evidence rating summary, Preschool Curriculum Evaluation Research (PCER) studies.
title: ELLM coaching cycle: coach models a lesson, teacher implements it, and written analysis of critical behaviors feeds a feedback and reflection conference

The coach first models a lesson demonstrating desired instructional behaviors while the teacher conducts a written analysis; a feedback and reflection conference asks "What worked? What needs to be added? What needs to be extended?". In the next cycle the teacher implements the lesson while the coach observes and analyzes the teacher's critical behaviors, followed by another conference in which coach and teacher plan the next cycle. Critical behaviors are specified in advance and analyzed during delivery.

One district staff member (~30 min/week) and one district-level data staff member (< 3 hrs total)
constraints: No professional development or training required beyond the stated staffing; no technology required
target_learners: Students at risk of chronic absenteeism and their parents/guardians
target_learning_goals: Reducing absences so students attend and benefit from instruction
examples: In both randomized evaluations, at-risk students' families received mailed, personalized Absence Reports while control families did not.

article_title: Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS)
citation: Faria et al. (2017). Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS). https://eric.ed.gov/?q=early+warning+intervention+and+monitoring+system
title: Early warning monitoring cycle: identify at-risk students with attendance, behavior, and course performance indicators, intervene, and monitor progress
description: The pattern is a recurring school-level cycle in which a dedicated team uses routinely collected indicators — "engagement (attendance), behavior (suspension), and course performance (grades and credits)" — to flag students at risk of not graduating on time, assign them to interventions, and monitor their progress over time. The model is intended to help schools efficiently use data to both identify the at-risk population and provide targeted support.
requirements: A dedicated school team to lead and carry out the process
Data on attendance, suspensions, grades, and credits
target_learners: High school students in grades 9 and 10
target_learning_goals: Student persistence and progress in school
On-time graduation
examples: In the evaluation, EWIMS schools used the indicators to identify at-risk students and assign interventions, yielding lower chronic absenteeism than usual-practice schools.
key_sources: Faria et al. (2017). Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS). https://eric.ed.gov/?q=early+warning+intervention+and+monitoring+system

article_title: Chapter One (Formerly Innovations for Learning High Impact Tutoring)
citation: Chapter One. (2024). Chapter One — Evidence Rating: Strong. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org/chapter-one
title: Push-in short-burst tutoring with personalized dosage
description: The program's instructional pattern places tutors inside the regular classroom rather than pulling students out: tutors "work with individual students in 5-10 minute increment sessions during blocks of reading instruction or other opportune moments." Session length and frequency vary by student need and rate of progress, with students needing more support meeting daily for periods of time. A student-relay handoff minimizes interruptions to classroom instruction.
requirements: Part-time tutors embedded in the classroom who serve multiple classrooms across the school
target_learners: kindergarten and first grade students needing supplementary reading support
target_learning_goals: phonics
reading fluency
examples: Students making adequate progress meet with their tutor once or twice a week, whereas students identified as needing more support may meet daily for periods of time
key_sources: Chapter One. (2024). Chapter One — Evidence Rating: Strong. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org/chapter-one

article_title: Early Learning in Mathematics
citation: Early Learning in Mathematics (ELM): Evidence Rating. (2021). https://www.evidenceforessessments.org/early-learning-in-mathematics/
title: Focused coverage of a small number of key mathematical ideas with explicit, systematic instruction
description: ELM's instructional design pattern emphasizes depth over breadth: "The curriculum emphasizes a small number of key ideas in math to provide more focused coverage, instead of trying to teach a comprehensive but more surface set of skills." It pairs this focused coverage with "Explicit and systematic instructional design." The pattern structures a full year of 120 45-minute lessons plus daily calendar activities.
requirements: A full year of structured lessons (120 45-minute lessons plus daily 15-minute calendar activities) delivered by the classroom teacher.
constraints: The review does not isolate which design feature produced the effects; the pattern is described, not experimentally decomposed.
target_learning_goals: core early mathematics concepts and skills
examples: ELM implements this pattern through 120 45-minute lessons and daily 15-minute calendar activities for the whole class.

article_title: Galaxy Math
citation: Galaxy Math. (2013). Program description, Evidence for ESSA. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Scripted one-to-one tutoring with fixed dosage and paraprofessional tutors
description: Galaxy Math operationalizes tutoring as a scripted, fixed-dosage, one-to-one delivery model: "The program is scripted, and tutors are expected to follow the scripts without reading them or memorizing them." Sessions are "30-minute sessions 3 times a week for 16 weeks" delivered by paraprofessionals, standardizing implementation across tutors.

2-day initial workshop plus weekly coordinator meetings
constraints: Designed for at-risk first graders in early arithmetic
target_learning_goals: addition and subtraction understanding and proficiency

article_title: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention
citation: PowerSchool Attendance Intervention. (2024). Evidence for ESI program review. https://www.evidenceforessi.org/
title: Automate personalization of family communication templates to reduce staff time burden
description: The review states that "[t]he ability to automatically populate a parent or student's name and real-time attendance data into communication templates greatly reduces the time burden for school staff." Attendance-communication tools should therefore pull names and live attendance data into message templates automatically, so educators can send accurate, personalized family messages at scale without manual entry.

target_learning_goals: Increasing family engagement and supporting student attendance
examples: The PowerSchool Attendance Intervention app auto-populates parent or student names and real-time attendance data into messaging templates used for two-way text and email communication with families.

article_title: Symphony Math
citation: Symphony Math. (2021). Symphony Math program description and evidence summary. https://www.symphonylearning.com
title: Require mastery of the current concept before advancing to the next in a sequenced math program
description: Symphony Math sequences mathematical concepts and does not let a student move on until the current concept is mastered. Because the time and practice students need is not uniform, the program lets students spend the time they need to master foundational concepts before progressing.
requirements: A sequenced progression of mathematical concepts with mastery assessment at each step
constraints: Requires allowing non-uniform amounts of time and practice per student
target_learning_goals: Mastery of foundational mathematical concepts
examples: A student does not move to the next concept in the Symphony Math sequence until she has mastered the current concept
key_sources: Symphony Math. (2021). Symphony Math program description and evidence summary. https://evidenceforessa.org/program/symphony-math/

article_title: Symphony Math
citation: Symphony Math. (2021). Symphony Math program description and evidence summary. https://www.symphonylearning.com
title: Adaptive pacing that accelerates to locate need then slows until understanding is achieved
description: The program quickly moves students through the conceptual progression to identify their area of need, then slows progress until the necessary understanding has been achieved. This two-phase pacing pattern combines rapid diagnosis with remedial slowdown, and also alerts educators when students show signs of struggle.
requirements: A conceptual progression of skills and ongoing performance monitoring to detect the area of need
target_learners: K-8 students needing individualized math practice
target_learning_goals: Identifying and remediating individual areas of need in mathematics
examples: Once the area of need has been identified, the program slows the progress until the necessary understanding has been achieved
key_sources: Symphony Math. (2021). Symphony Math program description and evidence summary. https://evidenceforessa.org/program/symphony-math/

article_title: eMINTS
citation: eMINTS (enhancing Missouri's Instructional Networked Teaching Strategies): Program description and evidence summary. (2023). Evidence for ESSA. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Build principal leadership and observation capacity alongside teacher professional development when implementing an instructional improvement program
description: eMINTS treats implementation leadership as part of the intervention itself: "The model also has a strong emphasis on helping principals understand and lead the program implementation and carry out teacher observations to support teachers' instructional performance." Professional development is thus directed not only at teachers but at principals and technology coordinators, so school leaders can understand, lead, and monitor the program rather than merely host it.
requirements: Principals receive professional development to understand and lead program implementation
Principals conduct teacher observations to support instructional performance
target_learning_goals: program implementation leadership
instructional quality through observation and support
examples: Professional development is provided to principals, technology coordinators, and classroom teachers in middle schools.
key_sources: eMINTS (enhancing Missouri's Instructional Networked Teaching Strategies): Program description and evidence summary. (2023). Evidence for ESSA. https://www.evidenceforessa.org

article_title: Pirate Math
citation: Pirate Math. (2021). Evidence for Learning program summary. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org.au
title: Token reward with mapped milestone prizes sustaining engagement across tutoring sessions
description: Pirate Math embeds a motivational routine in its tutoring sessions: students receive gold coins for good work and place them on a treasure map. When they reach a picture of a treasure box, they earn a small prize. This recurring reward cycle structures motivation across the 16-week program.
requirements: A treasure map and small prizes must be available across the 16-week session sequence
target_learners: Third graders in remedial math tutoring
target_learning_goals: Sustained engagement and effort in tutoring sessions
examples: Students receive gold coins for good work, place them on a treasure map, and earn a small prize on reaching the treasure box picture.

article_title: Pirate Math
citation: Pirate Math. (2021). Evidence for Learning program summary. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org.au
title: Deliver supplemental math tutoring one-to-one outside ordinary math periods, staffed by teachers or trained paraprofessionals
description: Pirate Math delivers tutoring one-to-one, with tutors who may be teachers or paraprofessionals working with students outside of ordinary math periods. This staffing and scheduling model allows struggling third graders to receive intensive individual support without displacing their regular math instruction.

constraints: Requires scheduling sessions outside ordinary math periods, three per week over 16 weeks
target_learning_goals: Math calculations and word problem solving

article_title: Evidence for ESSA: Zearn Math
citation: Zearn Math evidence review. (2024). https://zearn.org
title: Pair supplemental digital math programs with dedicated implementation support including professional development, coaching, and dosage monitoring
description: The review indicates that significant positive results occurred where Zearn Math was implemented with "accompanying professional development and coaching support for school leaders", which helps schools "establish dedicated time in the schedule for usage, build effective routines, and use data to ensure students reach the recommended dosage of three digital lessons per week". Support includes regular coach check-ins and motivational strategies such as classroom-based challenges to promote consistent lesson completion.
requirements: Dedicated scheduled time for program usage
Professional development and coaching for school leaders
Data-based progress monitoring toward the recommended dosage
Designated school or district points of contact for onboarding and rostering setup
constraints: The pilot implementation without full implementation support found no significant differences, suggesting support may be a boundary condition for effects.
target_learners: Students in grades K-8 in elementary and middle schools
target_learning_goals: Grade-level mathematics proficiency

article_title: Evidence for ESSA: OGAP Math Professional Learning System
citation: OGAP Math program description. (2024). Evidence for Learning. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org/ogap-math/
title: OGAP strand-based professional learning structure: cohorts of about 24 educators, four onsite days, and two follow-up coaching days
description: OGAP professional learning is organized by Strand, each aligned to a developmental progression in mathematics: Additive Reasoning (K–2), Multiplicative Reasoning (3–5), Fractional Reasoning (3–6), and Proportional Reasoning (6–8). Each strand is delivered to educator cohorts, often around 24 participants, through four onsite professional learning days, with districts able to space sessions several weeks apart. Two onsite follow-up coaching days, often during PLC time, "support transfer into classroom practice." Multiple strands may run simultaneously under the same structure.
requirements: Cohorts of about 24 educators per OGAP Strand
Four onsite professional learning days per strand
Two onsite follow-up coaching days, often scheduled during PLC time
constraints: Districts may choose consecutive sessions or a split schedule, with flexibility to space the sessions several weeks apart
target_learners: K–8 mathematics teachers participating in OGAP strands
target_learning_goals: Transfer of professional learning into classroom practice
Grade-band mathematical reasoning progressions (additive, multiplicative, fractional, proportional)
examples: Strands are aligned to grade-band progressions such as Multiplicative Reasoning (3–5) and Proportional Reasoning (6–8)

article_title: Evidence for ESSA: Graspable Math — From Here to There (FH2T)
citation: From Here to There (FH2T): Program Description and Evaluation Evidence. (2023). https://www.evidenceforlearning.org.au/the-toolkit/from-here-to-there/
title: Expression-transformation puzzle: match a starting expression to an equivalent target form via valid operations
description: The core design pattern of FH2T is a transformation puzzle: "The program presents a starting expression and a mathematically equivalent target expression. Students manipulate the original expression to match the target form." Because moves must be "mathematically valid operations," students practice algebraic manipulation by direct interaction with notation rather than by answering discrete items. The pattern embeds practice of distribution, factoring, inverse operations, and order of operations inside the game's goal structure.
requirements: A starting expression paired with a mathematically equivalent target expression
An interface allowing students to drag and transform expressions using mathematically valid operations
constraints: Applied in the article to algebraic expressions and equation solving for introductory prealgebra/algebra
target_learners: Middle and high school students learning introductory prealgebra or algebra
target_learning_goals: Fluency with algebraic manipulation operations, including distribution, factoring, inverse operations, and order of operations
examples: FH2T tasks ask students to transform a given expression into a target form using operations such as distribution and factoring.

Adaptivity operates within games, between games, and across the system to give "a customized pathway between skills based on prior performance," with cohesive narrative and interactive characters supporting engagement.

constraints: Designed for pre-kindergarten through second grade number sense and operations content

title: Three-level developmental progression of word-recognition instruction with an older-student variant

A separate variant, SIPPS Plus, covers the simple alphabetic and spelling-pattern phases but is designed specifically for older students in grades 4–12, allowing the same progression to serve adolescent struggling readers.

target_learning_goals: Progression from simple alphabetic to spelling-pattern to polysyllabic/morphemic word recognition

article_title: SIPPS (Systematic Instruction in Phonological Awareness, Phonics, and Sight Words)
citation: SIPPS program description and outcomes review. (2022). https://www.evidenceforessa.org/
title: Use placement and embedded mastery tests to drive grouping, pacing, and reteaching decisions
description: The article describes an assessment system in which "Assessment data determines placement in the program" and flexible groups based on placement results provide differentiated instruction. Criterion-referenced mastery tests embedded at designated intervals document mastery of phonics and high-frequency words and "support instructional decisions to guide reteaching, which may include adjusting pacing and delivery." This keeps instruction matched to individual progress through an accelerative scope and sequence.
requirements: Initial and ongoing assessment; criterion-referenced mastery tests embedded at designated intervals in each level's scope and sequence
target_learners: K-12 students in differentiated small groups within a foundational reading program

article_title: Expository Reading and Writing Course (ERWC)

title: ERWC instructional focus on discussion, critical thinking, oral language, genre writing, and rhetorical analysis

These foci operate across the whole twelfth-grade English course.

critical thinking
academic writing
oral language
rhetorical analysis

Content is organized across 19 content-based levels spanning subjects such as science, math, and social studies, and teachers receive real-time progress data with aligned small-group lesson plans.

Teachers review performance data and deliver small-group lessons

18 hours of professional development plus frequent staff development sessions and coaching from the developers
constraints: Positive outcomes should not be expected without the same level of professional development
target_learners: Spanish-speaking early readers in elementary grades
target_learning_goals: Accelerating the transition to reading in English
examples: In the research schools, intervention teachers received 18 hours of professional development, in addition to frequent staff development sessions and coaching.

article_title: JUMP Math
citation: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://www.jumpmath.org
title: Reduce math concepts to small steps to mastery, then build back up incrementally
description: In JUMP Math, "Math concepts are reduced to increasingly smaller steps until students achieve mastery, then built back up incrementally to meet the curriculum demands." Students receive extensive practice at each step. This stepwise reduction-and-rebuild structure is the core instructional mechanism of the program's guided-discovery approach.
requirements: Extensive practice at each step before moving on
target_learning_goals: mastering math concepts and meeting curriculum demands
examples: The program's teachers guides move students towards discovering target concepts through the sequence of small steps.
key_sources: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/jump-math/

article_title: JUMP Math
citation: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://www.jumpmath.org
title: Use ongoing assessment to ensure comprehension before moving to new material
description: JUMP Math treats assessment as continuous: "Assessment is ongoing and considered essential to ensure comprehension before moving on to new material." This gates progression on demonstrated understanding rather than fixed pacing, complementing the program's stepwise mastery structure and individual pacing within a shared class concept.
requirements: Ongoing assessment embedded in the lesson sequence
target_learning_goals: comprehension of math concepts before progression
examples: Students do easier or more challenging work, or gain more practice, relating to the lesson concept until they are ready to move on.
key_sources: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/jump-math/

article_title: JUMP Math
citation: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://www.jumpmath.org
title: Use concrete models strategically and remove them as soon as students can work without them
description: JUMP Math uses "a range of models (concrete materials, tables, diagrams) ... strategically to help students grasp abstract concepts but the models are removed as soon as students are able to work without these supports." The principle is deliberate, temporary scaffolding: models support abstraction but are faded promptly rather than retained.
requirements: Concrete materials, tables, or diagrams available to support abstract concepts
target_learning_goals: grasping abstract math concepts
examples: The program's practice of removing models as soon as students can work without supports.
key_sources: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/jump-math/

article_title: JUMP Math
citation: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://www.jumpmath.org
title: Streamline student materials and reserve lesson detail for teacher guides to protect working memory
description: JUMP Math has no student textbooks; students complete work in "practice and assessment guides that are streamlined to limit extraneous information and contain only the essential language." Lesson details are reserved for teachers' guides "so that teachers can control the timing and amount of information the students receive so as not to overwhelm student working memory."
requirements: Detailed teachers guides separate from streamlined student guides
target_learning_goals: reducing extraneous load while learning math concepts
examples: Smart board materials are not required but many teachers choose to use them.
key_sources: JUMP Math — Evidence Rating: Promising. (2023). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/jump-math/

article_title: Evidence for ESSA: Peer-Assisted Learning Strategies (PALS) — Reading
citation: Peer-Assisted Learning Strategies (PALS). (2001). Evidence Rating: strong. https://www.evidenceforessuccess.org
title: Turn-taking paired tutoring with structured literacy skill sequence and simple peer error correction
description: The PALS instructional pattern organizes children in reciprocal pairs who alternate roles, so each child experiences both tutoring and tutored practice across "a structured sequence of literacy skills". Peer interaction is structured by "a simple error correction strategy with each other, under guidance of a teacher", keeping correction in students' hands while the teacher oversees. The pattern spans phonemic awareness through story retelling.
requirements: Teacher guidance of the peer error correction strategy
On-site coaches needed
constraints: Teachers were least favorable about some components of the program’s team-based structure, such as announcing the winning team and the point structure
target_learning_goals: Phonemic awareness, phonics, sound blending, passage reading, and story retelling
examples: Program components include Sounds and Words, Pretend Read, Partner Read-Aloud, and Retell, which teachers rated highly in the Mathes & Babyak (2001) survey
key_sources: Peer-Assisted Learning Strategies (PALS). (2001). Evidence Rating: strong. https://www.evidenceforessuccess.org

article_title: Evidence for ESSA: Enhanced Core Reading Instruction (ECRI)
citation: Enhanced Core Reading Instruction. (2017). Evidence review summary. https://www.evidenceforesight.org
title: Align Tier 2 supplemental reading instruction with Tier 1 core instruction through teacher professional development and materials
description: The program's central design principle is alignment: it provides "teachers with professional development and materials to improve the alignment of Tier 2 with Tier 1 core instruction." Core reading teachers also receive professional days on the same strategies, so both tiers teach the same content with shared routines.
requirements: Professional development for both core teachers and small-group instructors (three days in total)
Professional development workbooks and a Leadership Guide
target_learning_goals: foundational reading skills, vocabulary, and comprehension aligned with the Common Core State Standards
examples: In the studied program, all students received 90 minutes of core reading instruction and 30 minutes of Tier 2 instruction, with Tier 2 preteaching the core content.
key_sources: Enhanced Core Reading Instruction. (2017). Evidence review summary. https://www.evidenceforesight.org

article_title: Evidence for ESSA: Enhanced Core Reading Instruction (ECRI)
citation: Enhanced Core Reading Instruction. (2017). Evidence review summary. https://www.evidenceforesight.org
title: Tiered reading delivery pattern: 90 minutes whole-group core plus 30 minutes small-group Tier 2 for all struggling readers
description: The studied program used a tiered time structure: "all students, experimental and control, received 90 minutes of core reading instruction and 30 minutes of Tier 2 (supplemental) instruction." Core instruction is whole group with classroom teachers; intervention occurs in small groups of 3-5 students led by teachers or instructional assistants.
requirements: Classroom teachers deliver whole-group core instruction
Teachers or instructional assistants deliver small-group Tier 2 intervention
constraints: The program does not require technology
target_learners: first grade students, including struggling readers
target_learning_goals: foundational reading skills delivered through aligned core and supplemental instruction
examples: In the Oregon and Massachusetts study, both experimental and control students received the same 90-minute core block and 30-minute Tier 2 block.
key_sources: Enhanced Core Reading Instruction. (2017). Evidence review summary. https://www.evidenceforesight.org

article_title: PAX Good Behavior Game — Math
citation: PAX Good Behavior Game. (2021). Evidence Rating. https://www.evidencebasedprograms.org/programs/pax-good-behavior-game/
title: Team-based group contingency with checkmarks and small privileges to encourage peer support for appropriate behavior
description: The pattern divides students into two or more teams and applies a group contingency: when a team member violates class rules, the team receives a checkmark on the whiteboard, and the team with the fewest checkmarks, or all teams meeting a criterion, receives a small privilege such as lining up first for recess. The summary states "This group contingency is intended to create a situation in which students encourage and assist their peers to behave appropriately."
requirements: Class rules must be discussed and agreed upon by the students themselves
Teacher monitoring of student behavior during lessons
constraints: Privileges are small, such as the opportunity to line up first for recess
target_learning_goals: self- and peer-regulation of classroom behavior
examples: Teams receive checkmarks on the whiteboard for rule violations; the winning team or all teams meeting criterion line up first for recess.
key_sources: PAX Good Behavior Game. (2021). Evidence Rating. https://www.evidencebasedprograms.org/programs/pax-good-behavior-game/

article_title: Just Right Reader Take-Everywhere Literacy Packs — Family Engagement
citation: Just Right Reader Take-Everywhere Literacy Packs™. (2025). Evidence review summary. https://www.justrightreader.com
title: Personalized, relevant decodable texts with named students and meaningful storylines to foster ownership and reading identity

The article states "This personalized and relevant design fosters ownership, increases engagement and confidence, and supports the development of strong reading identities."
requirements: Books must be matched to each student's phonics skill level and personalized with the student's name.
target_learning_goals: reading engagement
reading confidence
reading identity
phonics practice
examples: Packs include writing pages that connect reading and writing practice.

article_title: Thinking Math! by Innovamat
citation: Thinking Math! (Innovamat core curriculum) evidence rating summary. (2025). https://www.innovamat.com
title: Curriculum design combining learning progressions, CPA model, and spaced/interleaved practice
description: The curriculum is "built around research-based learning progressions, a Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract model, and rich mathematical activities designed to connect concepts, interleave and space practice for long-term retention, and provide meaningful contexts for learning." This design pattern organizes content sequencing, activity design, and practice scheduling across the PreK-8 program.
requirements: Teacher lesson guides and manipulative materials to enact the progression-based, CPA-aligned activities
target_learning_goals: Long-term retention of mathematics concepts
Connected conceptual understanding

article_title: Parent Teacher Home Visits
citation: Academic Performance — Parent Teacher Home Visits. (2021). Evidence summary. https://www.evidenceforesscp.org
title: Two-visit home visit structure: relationship-building first, academics second
description: PTHV organizes home visits as a two-visit sequence embedded in ongoing communication. The first visit is relationship-building and occurs in the summer or early fall; a second visit later focuses on academics or another relevant issue for the student or family. The page describes it as "a two-visit model, PTHV encourages the first relationship-building visit to occur in the summer or early fall, followed by ongoing communication throughout the year."
requirements: Visits are voluntary and arranged in advance
Teachers are trained and compensated for visits
target_learning_goals: Building teacher-family relationships and improving instruction for the learner
examples: Educators listen, ask questions, and make observations during visits that they take back to their classrooms to improve instruction.

article_title: Connect Science
citation: Connect Science program description and evidence rating summary. (2022). https://www.connectscience.org
title: Service-learning integrated elementary science unit pattern combining NGSS practices, collaborative skills, and a service project
description: This pattern organizes an elementary science unit around three integrated strands: standards-aligned science instruction, explicit social and collaborative skills teaching, and a facilitated service-learning experience. The article describes Connect Science as designed "to prepare teachers to use Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) instructional practices, teach social and collaborative skills, and facilitate a service-learning experience in their science class." The sequence of 31 lessons runs 14 weeks or more and can be integrated with other content instruction.
requirements: Teacher professional development prior to implementation
science materials kit and trade books accompanying the lessons
constraints: Designed for fourth grade; lessons replace existing science units
target_learning_goals: science achievement
social and collaborative skills
service-learning participation
examples: The evaluation implemented the pattern as 30 lessons of 30-50 minutes each over 14-22 weeks, compared against business-as-usual science instruction.
key_sources: Connect Science program description and evidence rating summary. (2022). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/connect-science/

article_title: Connect Science
citation: Connect Science program description and evidence rating summary. (2022). https://www.connectscience.org
title: Adopt Connect Science without additional staffing, using existing classroom teachers trained through its professional development
description: The program is designed to be delivered by regular classroom teachers rather than added personnel: the article states "No additional staffing requirements." Implementation instead depends on teacher preparation through the staged professional development sequence and provision of a manual, science materials kit, and trade books, making adoption a matter of teacher training and materials rather than new hires.
requirements: Teachers complete the professional development sequence and receive the lesson manual and materials kit
constraints: Teachers will need computers to access the web for videos, resources etc.
target_learning_goals: science achievement through NGSS-aligned, service-learning instruction
examples: In the cluster randomized evaluation, treatment classroom teachers delivered the lessons after summer professional development, with no additional staff reported.
